# osauer.dev · Software for a clearer portfolio

Updated: 2026-10-03

Personal software by Oliver Sauer: markets, applied AI and Go systems. The site
shows independent projects. It is not investment advice and makes no claim of
investment performance. Public screenshots use synthetic simulation data.

- [Canary Desk](https://osauer.dev/desk/): A private portfolio workspace preview.
  Market briefs, an AI analyst, risk rules and statement-backed FX contribution
  for Day, WTD, MTD and YTD. Its cash-sweep planner considers same-currency bills
  after commitments and liquidity reserves; it is off by default and requires
  owner commissioning, calibrated policy and current native settlement evidence.
  Order authority is separate from analysis: owner confirmation or explicitly
  scoped prior authority, with Canary's execution gates. The analyst remains
  read-only. Access is arranged personally; there is no commercial service or
  public Desk installer.
- [Canary CLI](https://osauer.dev/canary/): Desk's open-source broker engine,
  written in Go. A native TWS protocol implementation, daemon, CLI, read-only MCP
  tools and paired app. Standard downloads and all MCP tools cannot place orders.
  FX contribution is available in Canary v3.16.0 and Desk's private runtime. `canary reporting fx --json` and
  `canary_reporting_fx` expose statement-day
  currency valuation contribution, separately from realised Forex lot P&L.
  Incomplete periods disclose gaps and omit a total.
- Lending observations are available in Canary v3.16.0. Dated stock loans appear in position evidence;
  `canary lending fees --json` and `canary_lending_fees` expose bounded earned
  customer net-fee history. The Canary app
  adds position annotations and expandable fees, and Desk's analyst can read
  the evidence. Coverage distinguishes missing, partial and complete zero.
  Participation remains with IBKR. Fees do not get added to account P&L; payment
  and P&L linkage remain unproved. Populated account evidence is still needed
  for commissioning. Use v3.16.0 or later for these reporting features.
- [HyperServe](https://osauer.dev/hyperserve/): An open-source Go HTTP server
  library built around net/http, with optional MCP.
- [Torok](https://osauer.dev/torok/): The private Go agent runtime behind Canary
  Desk's morning briefs and AI analyst; it saves a run's progress as it goes.
- [Tower](https://osauer.dev/tower/): A private experiment in coordinating coding
  agents, switched off since 29 September 2026. No public download.

availability. Current source, private installed runtime and public release are
different evidence. Desk, Torok and Tower remain private.
